where: Section 2, bullet on counting sign changes
problem: It says "Zero sign changes means every root is in the left half plane, so the system is stable." That is false when roots lie on the jω axis. A polynomial with a factor such as s² + 11 gives a row of zeros, and after the auxiliary-row replacement the first column can show no sign changes while the roots are on the imaginary axis. The chapter itself contradicts this line: at K = 66 in the worked example and in Q8 the array has no sign changes yet the system is only marginally stable and oscillates.
fix: "The number of sign changes equals the number of roots in the right half plane. Zero sign changes means no root is in the right half plane. If no zero row and no zero first-column entry occurred, every root is strictly in the left half plane and the system is stable; if an auxiliary row was needed, zero sign changes means the system is marginally stable, with the jω-axis roots given by A(s) = 0."

problem: The sentence "If the whole row is not zero, this is the correct limiting process" is vague; a student may read it as a condition on the ε method rather than as the statement that distinguishes case 1 (one zero in the first column) from case 2 (all-zero row).
fix: "Use ε only when at least one other entry in that row is nonzero; if the whole row is zero, use Special case 2 instead."

problem: The question calls the array "completed" and then gives a first column that contains a zero, so the wording contradicts itself; the array is not complete until the ε process is done.
fix: "The first column of a Routh array, built directly from the coefficients, reads 1, 3, 0, 2, 5. Can you say there is one sign change? ..."

problem: The s² row has an empty third cell while the s³ row shows an explicit 0 in the same padding position; read against worked example step 1, students may think an entry is missing rather than zero.
fix: Show the third cell of row s² as 0, matching the padding used in the s³ row: cells ['1', '5', '0'].
